html:
Pedro II was the second and last emperor of Brazil, reigning from 1831 to 1889. He came to the throne at five, when his father Pedro I left for Portugal, and ruled in person from 1840.

A shy, bookish ruler who loved science, he corresponded with Darwin, Pasteur and Victor Hugo. Under him Brazil had a stable parliamentary monarchy, a free press and growing coffee wealth, while its Spanish-speaking neighbours went through civil wars. He led Brazil through the Paraguayan War of 1864 to 1870.

He favoured the end of slavery, and his daughter Isabel signed the abolition law in 1888. Planters who lost their slaves turned against the monarchy, and on 15 November 1889 the army proclaimed a republic. He went into exile and died in Paris two years later.
